Subject: Recap + TCO: Redwood vs hyperscaler inference (next tests)

Thanks again for the demo today, Emily
great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary of needs
- Low-latency text generation for customer-facing chat (P95 target ~250ms)
- High throughput batch processing for offline summarization jobs
- Strong data controls (VPC + KMS) for regulated data

Competitive notes we discussed
- Hyperscalers (Managed endpoints): easier procurement but higher per-token price at scale and less predictable tail latency; limited KV cache behavior.
- Other inference APIs: often cheaper list price but require heavy ops to hit predictable latency and cost.

Action items / next tests (my suggestion)
1) Unit-economics spike test (short): run 100k tokens over your real prompts with 2 batching configs (B1 small batch = 4, B2 large batch = 32) to measure effective per-1M-token cost extrapolation.
2) Full TCO run: 1M tokens (production-like prompts) with KV cache enabled vs disabled to estimate cache hit benefits.
3) Latency characterization: 1k parallel realtime requests to measure P50/P95/P99.

Attachments: I've attached an initial unit-econ workbook (redwood-unit-econ-1Mtokens.xlsx) with sample calc and a proposed mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan.docx).

Proposed schedule: start tests next week (Mar 16)
if that works we can lock in lambdas for SE time.

Thanks
I can set this up and loop Marcus for the test harness/measurement plan.

Best,

Emily
good questions. High-level apples-to-apples numbers (ballpark) below. Full workbook attached for your finance team (redwood-unit-econ-1Mtokens.xlsx).

Assumptions:
- Model: open-llm-mosaic-7B (quantized) representative for your workload
- Avg seq length: 350 tokens per request
- Batch configs: B1=4, B2=32
- KV cache: average prefix reuse 30% for dialog workloads (we'll test 0/30/60% scenarios)

Per-1M-token effective cost (approx)
- Redwood hosted (optimized batching + KV cache, B2): $480 per 1M tokens
- Redwood hosted (no cache, B1): $1,100 per 1M tokens
- AWS SageMaker (g5/inf1 typical config, no KV cache): $1,900 per 1M tokens
- Other inference API (unmanaged): $1,300 per 1M tokens

Key drivers
- Batching increases throughput and lowers amortized compute per token; effective cost falls sharply with larger batches for non-realtime bulk jobs.
- KV cache hit rate saves generated context compute; for dialog with 30% prefix reuse we typically see 20-35% token-level cost reduction; at 60% reuse the savings are >40%.
- Tail latency: Redwood routes small, low-parallel interactive traffic to lower-latency pools and can meet P95 ~200-300ms for 350-token sequences with the right model/hardware. Hyperscaler endpoints often have higher 95/99 tails under bursty loads unless you reserve capacity.

Proposed concrete test plan (we can run this with Marcus as SE):
- Quick baseline (Mar 16): 100k tokens, B1 & B2, cache off/on. Deliverable: per-1M extrapolated cost, P50/P95 latency distribution, and cache hit delta.
- Full TCO (Mar 18-19): 1M tokens, production prompt set, real concurrency. Deliverable: final per-1M cost range and MAP updates.

Attachments: redwood-unit-econ-1Mtokens.xlsx (detailed assumptions), mutual-action-plan.docx (timeline, responsibilities).

If that timeline works, I'll book the slots and Marcus will share the test harness details.

Thanks,
Aditya

Hi Emily
Marcus here (SE). Wanted to add technical detail so the experiments are unambiguous.

Test harness notes:
- We'll provide a small runner (k8s job + sample client) that replays your production prompts and measures token-level metrics.
- Batching config: we'll test micro-batch (B=4, latency-oriented) and throughput batch (B=32) and measure effective per-token GPU utilization.
- Cache tests: we will simulate prefix reuse at 0%, 30%, and 60% using your dialog logs; that will show delta on token generation compute.

Expected numbers (350-token average)
- P50 latency (B=4): ~90-140ms; P95: ~210-300ms depending on concurrency and hardware pinning.
- P50 latency (B=32 non-realtime): ~40-80ms; P95 increases if concurrency spikes but overall cost per token lower.
- Cache hit effect: 30% prefix reuse => ~25% cost improvement; 60% => ~45% improvement (these are conservative).

I'll upload the runner and a sample config to the Drive link in the MAP. If you can share a short anonymized prompt sample (100 entries) we can pre-run sanity checks before the 100k run.

Cheers,
